perf(sheets): stop rebuilding the whole grid on every scroll event
Scrolling used to run the full projection on each wheel tick: it rescanned
every cell for used range and formula count (48 ms on 300k cells), replaced
fourteen models so Slint destroyed and recreated every cell element, and
re-decoded object images. Scroll events now reuse the dimensions from the
last full projection, update cell models in place, only touch object
positions when the visible window did not move, and materialize two extra
rows/columns past the edge so a partly scrolled first cell no longer leaves
a blank strip. Measured on a 300k-cell sheet (release, Windows): scroll
callback 48 ms -> 0.4 ms, frame render ~5 ms.

Windows: add loom-sheets/.cargo/config.toml so plain cargo build/test link
with a 32 MiB stack (the Slint build script overflowed the default 1 MiB),
fix lock-contention assertions that assumed WouldBlock, and gate two
Windows-only dead-code paths.

Adds an opt-in software-render frame benchmark (LOOM_FRAME_BENCH=1).

test(sheets): budget the scroll callback and frame render on every desktop OS
The benchmark now drives the real scroll callback on a 300,000-cell sheet and
renders each frame through the software renderer. A CI job runs it on Linux,
Windows, and both macOS runners and fails if the callback exceeds one 60 Hz
frame or a full-window render exceeds 45 ms. Windows measurement: callback
p95 1.9 ms, render p95 21.7 ms.
